title: Choose the visual world for AgentBazaar
question: Your brief pinned the MercadoLibre marketplace language, and a pinned brief beats the roll. So the lead card is that world, raised by four disciplines the challengers donated. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Mercado
options.thesis: A dense trading floor that behaves like a shop you already know how to use.
options.viewport: Amber chrome over a four-up listing grid, each card carrying price, condition grade and the seller's opaque agent ID, with a live market strip above it.
options.risk: Familiar by construction; without the raises it degrades into a generic shop and loses the trading-floor seriousness the escrow model needs.

raised.raise: Every colour gets exactly one declared job and the page ships a legend; violet is reserved for the trade you are currently following and nothing else ever uses it.
Saturated colour is quarantined to state meaning only, so chrome, cards and canvas stay neutral and a coloured pixel always means something.
Every credit amount, agent ID and audit hash sets in true tabular numerals that align across rows, so columns of money read as a column.
On the security page every claim is pinned to the live artifact that proves it, never to prose.

options.label: The Settlement Sheet
options.thesis: The market as a clearing house ledger where every row is a position awaiting settlement.
options.viewport: A full-width settlement table of open positions, unsettled rows carrying an amber value-date stamp, with the ledger conservation figure held in the masthead.
options.risk: Cold and institutional; it reads as finance infrastructure rather than a marketplace, and the device being sold almost disappears.

options.label: Orienteering Map and Legend
options.thesis: A fixed colour terrain of market state with one reserved ink riding above it as the active trade.
options.viewport: Market state as a fixed colour language beneath, with the purple course line tracing one agent's path control-to-control through a negotiation.
options.case: Wins on product clarity: a course layer that never edits the terrain is literally our read-only constraint, and control-to-control maps onto the escrow lifecycle. Loses audience identification, since a buyer scanning phones is not reading a map.
options.risk: The map metaphor fights the shopping task and buries the device behind notation.

options.label: One Neutral Scale
options.thesis: Near-black on near-white with a single accent, where every claim is immediately followed by the interface detail proving it.
options.viewport: A restrained neutral market view where the only colour is the accent marking live state, each figure paired with the artifact that proves it.
options.case: Wins on product clarity for the security page, where claim-and-proof pairing is exactly the argument we have to make. Loses audience identification: a marketplace with no colour reads as developer tooling, and the mode rules call grey-plus-one-accent the category default without the category's polish.
options.risk: Four trade states cannot be told apart without colour, which breaks both scanning and the AA requirement.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Pure black and white data density with no colour at all.
options.viewport: Barcode columns of listings with monospace figures packed into the margin.
options.case: Loses both axes: no colour means four trade states collapse into one another, and it reads as an installation rather than a market.
options.kept: Tabular rigour, now donated to the lead direction.
options.risk: Unreadable state and an automatic AA failure.

options.label: Lexicon Shoulder and Plate
options.thesis: Dense entries at a fixed measure with all colour quarantined inside bordered plates.
options.viewport: Listings as ranked lexicon entries under guide words naming the span in view.
options.case: Loses both axes: a marketplace is not a reference work, and ranking entries by apparatus fights a grid built for price comparison.
options.kept: Colour quarantine, now donated to the lead direction.
options.risk: Scholarly to the point of unusable for a buying decision.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One listing owns the entire viewport, the next one a snap away.
options.viewport: A single device filling the screen with a right rail of actions.
options.case: Loses both axes: a marketplace is fundamentally comparison, and one-item-per-viewport destroys the density that makes comparison possible.
options.kept: One item as a genuinely complete state, now donated to the trade timeline.
options.risk: Comparison becomes impossible and the human view stops being an overview.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms built cell by cell on a visible construction grid.
options.viewport: A market index set on an exposed modular armature.
options.case: Loses both axes: an exposed construction grid on a working screen is costume, and monumental letterforms steal space the listing grid needs.
options.kept: A real module everything snaps to, now donated as strict alignment discipline.
options.risk: Expression consumes the density the task requires.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What a marketplace ships, executed impeccably and without a point of view.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a shopper expects, at full craft and nothing more.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other marketplace by design.
